module_title: Pleadings, Ex-parte Decrees, and Execution Mechanics
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the practical staging of a civil suit. It details the rules of drafting Pleadings, what happens when a party fails to show up to court, and how a paper decree translates into real-world asset recovery through Execution.

core_concepts.title: Pleadings (Order 6), Plaint (Order 7) & Written Statement (Order 8)
core_concepts.description:
- Pleadings: Plaint + Written Statement (WS).
- Rule of Pleading (Order 6 Rule 2): You must state only **Material Facts**, and NOT the evidence by which they are to be proved. You must not plead the law.
- Plaint: The document filed by the Plaintiff to initiate the suit.
- Written Statement: The defense filed by the Defendant. Under Order 8 Rule 1, the WS must be filed within 30 days from the service of summons (extendable up to 90 days, and in commercial suits up to 120 days).

core_concepts.title: Set-off vs. Counter-claim (Order 8)
core_concepts.description:
Defensive weapons used by the Defendant.
- Legal Set-off (O8 R6): A cross-claim for an **ascertained (fixed) sum of money** legally recoverable from the plaintiff. It operates as a shield.
- Counter-claim (O8 R6A): The defendant can file a claim against the plaintiff for any right or claim arising before or after filing the suit. It does not have to be an ascertained sum. It operates as an independent 'sword' (a cross-suit).

core_concepts.title: Appearance and Non-Appearance (Order 9)
core_concepts.description:
What happens on the date of hearing?
- If neither party appears: Suit is dismissed (O9 R3).
- If ONLY Defendant appears: Suit is dismissed, unless the defendant admits the claim (O9 R8).
- If ONLY Plaintiff appears: The court may proceed **Ex-parte** and pass a decree against the absent defendant (O9 R6).
- Remedy for Ex-parte Decree: The defendant can apply under **Order 9 Rule 13** to set aside the ex-parte decree if they prove they were not duly served the summons or had 'sufficient cause' for non-appearance.

core_concepts.title: Execution of Decrees (Order 21)
core_concepts.description:
The longest order in the CPC, dealing with how to enforce the court's decree.
- Modes of Execution (Sec 51): Delivery of property, attachment and sale of property, or arrest and detention in civil prison.
- Protection against Arrest: Women, judicial officers, and members of legislative bodies (during session) cannot be arrested in execution of a money decree.

important_entities.name: Constructive Res Judicata (Section 11, Explanation IV)
important_entities.key_fact: You cannot hold back arguments for later.
important_entities.significance: A deeply tested concept. It states that any matter which *might and ought* to have been made a ground of defense or attack in the former suit shall be deemed to have been a matter directly and substantially in issue in that suit. You cannot file a new case claiming you 'forgot' to raise a specific point in the first case.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced exams test Section 60 (Property liable to attachment). In executing a money decree, can the court attach the entire salary of the judgment debtor? **NO**. Under Section 60(1)(i), the first Rs. 1,000 and two-thirds of the remainder of the salary are EXEMPT from attachment, ensuring the debtor has money to survive.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Order 6 is the Mix (Pleadings), Order 7 is Plaintiff's Heaven (Plaint), Order 8 is the Defendant's Gate (WS).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use the numerical sequence (6, 7, 8) to remember the flow from general rules to specific plaintiff and defendant documents.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary question asks 'Within what maximum period must a Written Statement be filed in a normal civil suit?', the answer is **90 days** (30 days default + 60 days extension for reasons recorded in writing).
